title: Audit-Log Generation Coverage & Continuity Across All In-Scope Systems
exclusions: Covers the audit-generation mechanism itself — that every in-scope system listed in the authoritative audit-source inventory is generating audit records and that no source has gone silent within the review window. It does NOT verify the integrity/immutability of stored log content (UC-22.35.2 WORM chain-of-custody, UC-22.35.3 replication), does NOT adjudicate whether an individual logged action was appropriate (the per-framework access/anomaly UCs), and does NOT cover audit *review/analysis* (that is the audit-review control). Test, sandbox, pre-production, and formally out-of-scope systems are excluded via the inventory lookup's `required` flag.
evidence: Saved search 'UC-22.35.6 — audit-source coverage & continuity' (scheduled to the documented review cadence) writes a per-source coverage record to the restricted audit_evidence index (default 7-year retention); the companion dashboard 'Audit-log generation coverage' provides the timestamped operating-effectiveness evidence an auditor reviews for the audit-generation/continuity obligations across NIST 800-53, SOX ITGC, PCI DSS, and HITRUST.

compliance.assurance_rationale: AU-12 requires that the system provide audit-record generation capability across the in-scope components and generate records for the AU-2 event types. This UC is the operating evidence of that capability end-to-end: it reconciles the authoritative audit-source inventory against live telemetry so that any in-scope component not generating audit records surfaces as an explicit GAP row, and it confirms continuity (no source gone silent) for every other source. Splunk is the sole-sufficient control that proves generation coverage is operating, so the grade is full; the orthogonal AU-12(b) 'allow personnel to select event types' configuration is a one-time admin setting outside detective scope.
compliance.controlObjective: Proves audit-record generation is operating across every in-scope system (AU-12), with any component that stops generating records flagged for follow-up.
compliance.evidenceArtifact: Saved search 'UC-22.35.6' reconciling live audit telemetry against audit_log_sources.csv, archived to the restricted audit_evidence index with a coverage_status column an assessor can read directly.

compliance.assurance_rationale: AU-2 (Event Logging) requires that the organization's defined event types are in fact logged across the in-scope systems. The operating evidence for that obligation is precisely what this UC produces: it reconciles the authoritative audit-source inventory against live telemetry, proving every in-scope source is generating audit records (and flagging any that has gone silent). The governance half of AU-2 — selecting which event types to log — is a documented administrative decision; the detective, sole-sufficient evidence that the selected events are being logged is this coverage-and-continuity control, so the grade is full.
compliance.controlObjective: Evidence that AU-2 event logging operates — the defined event types are being logged across every in-scope system, with any source not logging surfaced as a GAP.
compliance.evidenceArtifact: Saved search 'UC-22.35.6' audit-source coverage record archived to the restricted audit_evidence index, demonstrating the selected event types are being logged across in-scope systems.

compliance.assurance_rationale: Audit-trail completeness for ITGC depends on the relevant financial-system audit logs being captured without gaps across the reporting period. This UC is that completeness control: every in-scope financial/ERP/database audit source is reconciled against the inventory and any window with zero events (a feed that quietly stopped) is raised as a GAP, producing the per-period evidence an IT auditor needs to conclude the logging control operated. Splunk is the sole-sufficient mechanism for evidencing continuity, so the grade is full.
compliance.controlObjective: Evidence that the SOX ITGC logging-continuity control operates — every in-scope financial-system audit source is generating records continuously, with gaps flagged.
compliance.evidenceArtifact: Saved search 'UC-22.35.6' coverage-and-continuity record archived monthly to the restricted audit_evidence index for IT General Controls testing.

compliance.assurance_rationale: PCI DSS 10.2 requires that audit logs are captured (generated) for all system components in the cardholder-data environment. This UC is exactly the coverage control 10.2 calls for: the in-scope CDE component inventory is reconciled against live audit telemetry so any component not producing logs surfaces as a GAP, and continuity is confirmed for the rest. Splunk is the sole-sufficient control proving logs are captured for all components, so the grade is full; downstream log-content (10.2.1.x fields) and log-protection (10.5) are covered by separate UCs.
compliance.controlObjective: Evidence that PCI DSS 10.2 is satisfied — audit logs are captured for all in-scope CDE system components, with silent components flagged.

compliance.assurance_rationale: HITRUST CSF 09.aa (Audit Logging) requires that audit logs recording user activities, exceptions, and security events are produced and kept across in-scope systems. This UC is the operating control: it proves every in-scope system in the audit-source inventory is generating those logs and continuously forwarding them, flagging any silent source. Splunk is the sole-sufficient mechanism evidencing the logging requirement operates, so the grade is full.

controlTest.positiveScenario: UC-22.35.6 positive (Audit, Log, Generation, Coverage, Continuity): ingest synthetic events into `index=target_index` sourcetype='target_sourcetype' where `reporting_hosts`, `audit_events`, `last_event` grouped by `sourcetype` satisfies `audit_events` > 0, `gap_minutes` > 120, `in` > 2, or `audit_events` > 0 for 'Audit-Log Generation Coverage & Continuity Across All In-Scope Systems'.  Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row.
controlTest.negativeScenario: UC-22.35.6 negative (Scope Systems): ingest benign `target_index` / `target_sourcetype` events where `sourcetype` stays below `audit_events` > 0, `gap_minutes` > 120, `in` > 2, or `audit_events` > 0, or exclude the test entity via `compliance_exception_register.csv`. Variant 15 confirms zero alert rows for 'Audit-Log Generation Coverage & Continuity Across All In-Scope Systems'.

dataSources: Live audit telemetry across all in-scope indexes/sourcetypes (e.g. `WinEventLog:Security`, `mssql:audit`, `oracle:audit`, `linux_secure`, `aws:cloudtrail`, `o365:management:activity`) reconciled against the authoritative inventory lookup `audit_log_sources.csv` (columns: `sourcetype`, `component`, `owner`, `required`). Collected via Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud Platform (native; no premium app required). Reads the audit feeds already onboarded by the relevant Splunk technology add-ons for Windows, databases, Linux, and cloud platforms. (Splunkbase) — Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742)
spl:
| tstats count as audit_events, dc(host) as reporting_hosts, latest(_time) as last_event where index=* sourcetype=* earliest=-24h by sourcetype
| append [| inputlookup audit_log_sources.csv | eval audit_events=0]
| stats max(audit_events) as audit_events, max(reporting_hosts) as reporting_hosts, max(last_event) as last_event, values(component) as component, values(owner) as owner, values(required) as required by sourcetype
| where required="true" OR audit_events>0
| eval gap_minutes=round((now()-last_event)/60, 1)
| eval coverage_status=case(audit_events=0, "GAP - expected audit source silent in review window", gap_minutes>120, "STALE - no audit events in >2h", true(), "recording")
| eval component=coalesce(component, sourcetype)
| eval last_event=if(audit_events>0, strftime(last_event, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "never")
| eval reviewed_at=strftime(now(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
| table component, owner, sourcetype, audit_events, reporting_hosts, last_event, gap_minutes, coverage_status, reviewed_at
| sort coverage_status, - audit_events

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Authorised NIST 800 53 control testing** — Internal audit exercises 'Audit-Log Generation Coverage & Continuity Across All In-Scope Systems' (UC-22.35.6) on `sourcetype` during scheduled clause AU-12 sampling. Match compliance programme calendar.

2. **External assessor sampling** — QSA activity spikes `index=audit_evidence` `configured sourcetype` without crossing `audit_events` > 0. Cross-check engagement letter in `nist_800_53_exception_register.csv`.

3. **Planned maintenance affecting control telemetry** — CAB change pauses ingestion to `audit_evidence` for `sourcetype`. Compare `_time` with active change record.

4. **Third-party processor under contract** — BAA/DPA-covered vendor generates expected rows grouped by `sourcetype` during normal service delivery.

**Suppression mechanism:** `nist_800_53_exception_register.csv` keyed on `sourcetype`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`, joined before alert threshold.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Enterprise ≥9.2 or Splunk Cloud (current). No premium app is required — this control is platform-native and reads the audit feeds your other compliance UCs already onboard.
• **Audit feeds onboarded**: The in-scope systems must already forward audit logs into Splunk — Windows Security (`WinEventLog:Security`), database audit (`mssql:audit`, `oracle:audit`), Linux (`linux_secure`), and cloud control-plane (`aws:cloudtrail`, `o365:management:activity`) are the reference set; add the sourcetypes for any other in-scope system.
• **Inventory lookup**: `audit_log_sources.csv` must exist on the search tier with columns `sourcetype, component, owner, required`, one row per in-scope audit source (`required=true` for sources that must be recording). This file is the authoritative scope statement for the control — only sources listed and required here count toward coverage, so its accuracy is the control's foundation. Version it in source control and review it whenever a system is added or retired.
• **Indexes**: the in-scope audit indexes must exist with retention meeting the strictest applicable obligation (PCI DSS 12 months online / 3 months immediately available; SOX/HITRUST per policy) and a provisioned archive tier.
• **Regulatory mapping**: this control evidences NIST 800-53 `AU-12`, SOX ITGC `ITGC.Logging.Continuity`, PCI DSS `10.2`, and HITRUST `09.aa` simultaneously. Every result record carries `coverage_status` and `reviewed_at` so downstream consumers can read the audit-generation evidence directly.

## Step 1 — Build and own the audit-source inventory

The control can only prove completeness if it knows what *should* be reporting. Populate `audit_log_sources.csv` from the authoritative system inventory — every application, database, OS, and cloud control-plane feed that records security-relevant activity on an in-scope system. A minimum row is `sourcetype, component, owner, required`; set `required=true` for sources that must always be recording. Assign a named owner per source so GAP follow-up has an accountable recipient. Treat changes to this file as change-controlled: a source silently removed here disappears from the coverage denominator.

## Step 2 — Implement the search

The search has two halves that together evidence 'generated and continuous':

1. **Coverage (generation):** `tstats` counts audit events per in-scope sourcetype over the review window. Because `tstats` only returns sourcetypes that produced events, a fully-silent source would simply be absent — so the search `append`s the inventory with `audit_events=0` and then `stats max(...) by sourcetype`. The result is one row per *expected* source: a silent source survives as a zero-count row labelled `GAP`, which is the failure mode that matters most.
2. **Continuity (freshness):** the same row carries `last_event` and a derived `gap_minutes`; a source still present but stale beyond the freshness budget is labelled `STALE` before it becomes a full GAP.

This `append` + `stats` pattern is used deliberately instead of `join` so no expected source is silently dropped by subsearch truncation. Schedule a daily continuity run plus a monthly evidence snapshot:

```ini
[UC-22.35.6: Audit-Log Generation Coverage & Continuity]
cron_schedule = 0 6 * * *
dispatch.earliest_time = -24h
dispatch.latest_time = now
actions = summary_index
action.summary_index._name = audit_evidence
action.summary_index.marker = uc=22.35.6,controls=AU-12;ITGC.Logging.Continuity;PCI-10.2;HITRUST-09.aa
```

## Step 3 — Validate deployment

**(a) Inventory sanity:** confirm the lookup loads and has the expected row count:

```spl
| inputlookup audit_log_sources.csv
| stats count as inventory_sources, dc(sourcetype) as distinct_sourcetypes
```

**(b) Coverage dry-run:** run the base search and confirm every required inventory source appears exactly once and that recording sources show non-zero `audit_events`.

**(c) Negative test:** with all feeds healthy, confirm zero GAP/STALE rows (see controlTest negativeScenario).

**(d) Positive test:** pause one feed for the window and confirm it surfaces as a GAP row (see controlTest positiveScenario).

## Step 4 — Operationalize (dashboard and reporting)

Build the dashboard 'Audit-log generation coverage':

**Panel 1 — Single value:** '% of in-scope sources recording' = recording / required total. This is the headline audit-generation health number.

**Panel 2 — Coverage table:** component, owner, sourcetype, audit_events, gap_minutes, coverage_status — GAP/STALE rows highlighted red. This is the record an auditor reads for AU-12 / PCI 10.2 / SOX continuity / HITRUST 09.aa.

**Panel 3 — Activity trend:** `timechart` of audit_events per source so the reviewer can see collapses that stop short of a full GAP.

Enable scheduled PDF export on the review cadence and archive to the restricted audit_evidence index.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting and caveats

• **A source shows GAP but is healthy:** check the sourcetype string in `audit_log_sources.csv` matches the live sourcetype exactly (case-sensitive), and that its index is reachable by the search role.

• **Retention:** confirm the in-scope indexes meet the strictest applicable retention (PCI DSS requires 12 months with 3 months immediately searchable) and that the archive tier is provisioned — otherwise the evidence this control produces cannot itself be retained for the required period.

• **Scope discipline:** the control's credibility rests on the inventory. An in-scope system missing from `audit_log_sources.csv` is invisible to the coverage check; periodically reconcile the lookup against the authoritative asset inventory, not against index names alone.

**Ecosystem integration:** Forward compliance detections to Splunk SOAR for automated incident triage and escalation playbooks. Enrich events with asset context from ServiceNow CMDB. Cross-reference with CrowdStrike Falcon or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint for host forensics and threat detection context. Integrate Okta or Azure AD identity context to determine if the acting user had appropriate authorisation. Feed validated findings into the GRC platform (e.g., RSA Archer, ServiceNow GRC, or AuditBoard) for regulatory compliance tracking and audit evidence management.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud Platform (native; no premium app required). Reads the audit feeds already onboarded by the relevant Splunk technology add-ons for Windows, databases, Linux, and cloud platforms. (Splunkbase) — Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into index=main. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`audit_events, coverage_status, gap_minutes, in`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We keep a master list of every important system that should be writing down who did what, and we check every day that each one is still doing it. If any system quietly stops keeping its records, we spot the gap straight away instead of finding out during an audit.
